subject: ss-rheumatology-immunology
title: Sjogren disease: sicca, antibodies, glandular biopsy and lymphoma surveillance

steps.tx: Sjogren disease is a chronic autoimmune exocrinopathy in which lymphocytes infiltrate lacrimal and salivary glands. It presents with **keratoconjunctivitis sicca** (dry eyes) and **xerostomia** (dry mouth). Systemic features include fatigue, arthralgia, Raynaud phenomenon, parotid swelling and cutaneous vasculitis. Most patients have a slow, benign course, but lymphoma is the key threat.

steps.tx: Diagnosis rests on objective sicca plus supportive serology. Anti-Ro/SSA and anti-La/SSB antibodies are characteristic, alongside a positive **ANA** and **rheumatoid factor**. Schirmer test of 5 mm or less in 5 minutes supports diagnosis, and unstimulated whole saliva flow of 0.1 mL per minute or less scores. **Labial minor salivary gland biopsy** with focus score 1 or more per 4 mm squared is the most specific test.
steps.say: Diagnosis rests on objective sicca plus supportive serology. Anti-Ro SSA and anti-La SSB antibodies are characteristic, alongside a positive ANA and rheumatoid factor. A Schirmer test of 5 millimetres or less in 5 minutes supports the diagnosis, and unstimulated whole saliva flow of 0.1 millilitres per minute or less scores. Labial minor salivary gland biopsy with a focus score of 1 or more per 4 millimetres squared is the most specific test.

steps.tx: Lymphoma risk is the dominant long-term hazard. Sjogren carries the highest lymphoma risk of any autoimmune disease, mostly extranodal **MALT lymphoma**. Red flags include persistent unilateral parotid enlargement, a lymph node mass above 7 cm, new cytopenias, low C4, cryoglobulins and palpable purpura. Such features demand urgent investigation, not assumption of flare.

nodes.label: Lymph node above 7 cm or cytopenias

steps.tx: Renal and pregnancy issues matter. Interstitial nephritis may be silent, presenting only with **distal renal tubular acidosis**, which can progress to nephrocalcinosis if untreated. In pregnancy, anti-Ro antibodies risk neonatal lupus and **congenital heart block**, so fetal surveillance is needed. Consider HIV or HCV sicca, sarcoidosis and IgG4-related disease as mimics.

steps.tx: Management is symptomatic and multidisciplinary. Treat dry eyes with artificial tears, topical **ciclosporin** or lifitegrast, and punctal occlusion, trying plugs before cautery. Treat dry mouth with saliva substitutes and secretagogues such as **pilocarpine** or cevimeline. Hydroxychloroquine helps arthralgia and fatigue. Refractory systemic disease with vasculitis may need rituximab.
